note: One entry per screenshot on plantoir.app. `build.py` reads alt and caption to write the <picture> element; `website/shots/capture.py` reads `capture` to know how each is produced. Every shot is taken twice, once with the Mac in light appearance and once in dark, and saved as site/img/<id>-light.png and -dark.png. Paths are lowercase because Quartz serves lowercase URLs and 301s anything else — a capitalised address would be photographed mid-redirect.

shots.alt: Three overlapping windows in a diagonal cascade: Markdown notes in Obsidian on the left, Plantoir deploying the site in the middle, and the finished class website in Safari on the right.
shots.caption: From your notes in Obsidian, through Plantoir, to a live class website.

shots.alt: The Plantoir window listing three courses in a sidebar, with one section open beside it.
shots.caption: Every course and every class section, in one window.

shots.alt: The new course panel, with a course code entered and a summary of the pages about to be created.
shots.caption: Adding a course takes one panel and about a minute.

shots.alt: A progress view describing, in plain language, the step the site build has reached.
shots.caption: Progress is described in words, not in log output.

shots.alt: The Plantoir window with a class website shown inside it, beside the list of courses and sections.
shots.caption: The site, in the app, before anyone else has seen it.

shots.alt: The assistant window: a request typed in plain English, and the assistant describing what it is about to change with a button to approve it.
shots.caption: It says what it will do, then waits.

shots.alt: A Grade 10 English class website in a browser, with a navigation sidebar, a search field and a page of class notes.
shots.caption: What a class sees.

shots.alt: A Grade 12 Calculus and Vectors page opening with typeset mathematics: a displayed definition and a table of derivative rules.
shots.caption: The preview is the real site — equations and all.

shots.alt: A Grade 11 Chemistry page showing a flowchart beside the few lines of text that produced it.
shots.caption: Diagrams are written, not drawn — and edited in seconds.

shots.alt: The same class website at phone width, with the navigation collapsed behind a button.
shots.caption: The same site on a phone.

shots.alt: A grid of every curriculum expectation in a course, each square shaded by how many pages address it, with pale squares showing the gaps.
shots.caption: Every expectation in the course, shaded by how well it is covered.

shots.alt: A search panel open over a class website, listing matching pages with the search term highlighted in context.
shots.caption: One box, the whole course.

shots.alt: Three class websites overlapping like a fanned deck of cards, each in a different colour scheme and typeface.
shots.caption: Three courses, three colour schemes. Chosen in the app, not in code.

shots.alt: The same class website twice, side by side: once in a light colour scheme and once in a dark one.
shots.caption: And every site does both, whichever a student prefers.
